text:
Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is fine on a US flight, as long as it goes in your carry-on and not your checked bag.

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limit for spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks is 100 Wh each. To convert, divide mAh by 1,000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks are rated at about 3.7 V, so 20,000 mAh is about 74 Wh, well under the limit. Check the Wh figure printed on your bank, since some are rated slightly differently. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- The FAA sets no quantity limit for personal-use batteries under 100 Wh. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))

**Rules to follow**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare lithium batteries and power banks are not allowed in checked baggage. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep the bank in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over exposed terminals, so they can't touch metal. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Damaged or recalled banks can't fly.** Check for a recall before you go, since some Anker models were recalled in 2025. ([FAA: PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))
- **Tell the crew** right away if it gets hot, swells, or smokes. ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))

**Airline rules can be stricter**
The FAA says airlines may set tighter limits on how many power banks you can bring. A recent roundup of airline policies (a retailer's page, so check with your airline) lists the following ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying)):
- Southwest: one power bank per customer, and you can't charge it from seat power.
- American and Delta: two per passenger, with no recharging the bank on board.
- JetBlue: two per customer.
- Many airlines don't allow using a power bank in flight, or require it to stay visible while in use.

Check your airline's policy before you fly, especially if you're bringing more than one bank or flying internationally, where rules can be tighter.
